title: Research
text: I conducted a systematic RNA-seq meta-analysis of common bean stress transcriptomes (19 public datasets), combining statistical meta-analysis with machine learning and network-based gene discovery to identify consensus stress-responsive genes. I then evaluated whether SNP subsets prioritized by proximity to these evidence genes improve genomic prediction accuracy relative to standard equal-weight GBLUP and random-marker controls. This framework has been applied to bacterial wilt and soybean cyst nematode resistance in common bean, and, through cross-species ortholog mapping, to abiotic stress tolerance (drought, salt) in cowpea.

title: Research
text:
Disease resistance breeding and genetics
My graduate and industry work in plant pathology focused directly on disease-resistance breeding: breeding spinach for resistance to the downy mildew pathogen Peronospora effusa, including genetic characterization of resistance loci and race-specific resistance across worldwide germplasm, and three years evaluating field corn, sweet corn, and soybean for pathogen resistance within Syngenta’s Trait Assessment pipeline.

title: Research
section: Multi-breed genomic prediction in beef cattle
text:
Multi-breed genomic prediction in beef cattle
I built and validated a full genomic prediction pipeline for puberty and fertility traits (reproductive tract score, pelvic height and width, days open, heifer pregnancy) across five beef cattle breed populations: Angus, Red Angus, Hereford, a Bos indicus-influenced population, and a pooled MultiBreed population of over 9,000 animals genotyped on an 800K SNP panel. The pipeline covers univariate, bivariate, and multi-trait single-step GBLUP and GBLUP models via BLUPF90+/GIBBSF90+, with genetic parameter estimation (heritability, genetic correlations) via REML/AI-REML and prediction accuracy validated using the LR (Legarra & Reverter, 2018) temporal validation framework. Related work includes a Breed-As-Trait analysis estimating genetic correlations for the same traits across breeds, and a population-stratification-adjusted (PCA-corrected) extension of the MultiBreed models.

title: Dotun Olaoye
text:
I hold a Bachelor of Agriculture (Honors: Crop Protection/Pathology) from the Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta, Nigeria, and a Master of Science in Plant Breeding, Genetics and Pathology from the University of Arkansas, Fayetteville, where I worked on breeding spinach for resistance to the downy mildew pathogen Peronospora effusa, including genetic characterization of resistance loci and race-specific resistance across worldwide germplasm. During this period I also conceived the RNA-seq meta-analysis and cross-species genomic prediction framework I have continued to develop since, which uses machine learning and network analysis to identify stress-responsive genes in common bean and tests whether SNP subsets prioritized by these genes improve genomic prediction accuracy for disease-resistance traits in common bean and abiotic-stress traits in cowpea.
Between the master’s and my current PhD, I spent three years as a Pathology Research Specialist at Syngenta Seeds Inc., evaluating field corn, sweet corn, and soybean for resistance to economically important plant pathogens within a commercial trait-advancement pipeline.
I am a PhD student in Statistical Genetics at the University of Missouri, Columbia, working with Dr. Jared Decker in the Genetics Area Program. My current research centers on multi-breed genomic evaluation of puberty and fertility traits in beef cattle, using single-step GBLUP and GBLUP models.
Across these roles, my work combines statistical genetics methodology, including mixed-model genetic evaluation and LR validation, with a background in plant pathology and disease-resistance breeding, applied to problems in both livestock and crop improvement.

title: CV
text:
DATA/GENOMIC/STATISTICAL ANALYTICAL PROFICIENCY
Quantitative genetics / genomic prediction: Single-step GBLUP (ssGBLUP) and GBLUP via BLUPF90+/GIBBSF90+, including threshold models for binary traits; univariate, bivariate, and multi-trait mixed-model analyses; REML/AI-REML variance component estimation; heritability and genetic correlation estimation across multiple breed populations; genomic relationship matrix construction (VanRaden method)
Validation methodology: LR (Legarra & Reverter, 2018) temporal and cross-validation frameworks for genomic prediction accuracy, bias, and dispersion
Weighted/informed genomic prediction: SNP-weighting schemes informed by meta-transcriptomic (RNA-seq) evidence, applied to disease-resistance and abiotic-stress trait prediction in legume crops (cowpea, common bean)
Population genetics: Principal component analysis and population stratification correction (PLINK); genotype imputation (Beagle); variant filtering and manipulation (bcftools)
Programming/computation: R (sommer, lme4/lmerTest, tidyverse, ggplot2), Python, Perl, SQL, SAS, JMP, Quarto/R Markdown for reproducible reporting, shell scripting, HPC job orchestration (SLURM)
Genomic/bioinformatics tools: BLUPF90+/GIBBSF90+ family, PLINK, bcftools, Beagle, TASSEL, MEGA, QTL mapping and GWAS software, genomic selection models implemented in R
Experience working with large-scale sequence and genotype data, including 800K-SNP genotype panels and multi-breed populations exceeding 9,000 animals
